speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what expertise and resources does PUB have to understand, monitor and prevent midges outbreaks at reservoirs; (b) what are the key indicators that PUB uses to predict and pre-empt an outbreak; and (c) how can residents living near reservoirs be better protected from the outbreaks.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Non-biting midges, also known as chironomids, are a type of flying insect that thrive in water bodies, such as ponds, rivers and reservoirs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Midges are part of natural aquatic ecosystems and they are food for fishes and birds.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Midges can multiply very rapidly, with each female adult midge laying up to 500 eggs in the water bodies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The eggs take a few days to hatch and become larvae, which live at the bottom of the reservoir.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: After about two weeks, they develop to become pupae, swim to the water surface and emerge as adults.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The adult midges live for only one to two days, during which time they remain above water bodies to mate and lay eggs to continue their lifecycle.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Midges' emergence occurs from time to time in several reservoirs, including Pandan, Bedok, Punggol, Serangoon, Poyan, Tengeh and Marina reservoirs, as well as Punggol Waterway.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Midge emergence has been known to occur at Pandan Reservoir since the late 1970s.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Each emergence can be as brief as two weeks or as long as five months.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There are several factors that determine the scale and duration of each emergence, including the specific midge species and the environmental conditions, such as rainfall, temperature and water chemistry at time of the emergence.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have just experienced a period of hot weather, with July being the second warmest July recorded since 1929.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This unusual hot spell hastened the midges' growth process, resulting in the situation at Pandan Reservoir.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With climate change, we will experience more extreme weather, which will have a corresponding response from nature.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But they pose a nuisance to the public when they swarm in large numbers and, being weak flyers, get blown by wind into the surrounding residential estates.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Public Utilities Board (PUB) takes a comprehensive suite of measures to mitigate this nuisance factor as far as is feasible.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB monitors for midge emergence at reservoirs with known emergence by conducting frequent checks for larvae in samples of reservoir sediments or adult midges trapped around the reservoir vicinity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Similar to what I explained to this House previously in 2016, PUB's mitigation measures for midges include increasing the frequency and dosage of the application of biological liquid larvicide within the reservoir to kill midge larvae and increasing the frequency of fogging and misting around the reservoir dyke and surrounding vegetation to kill adult midges.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These methods have proven to kill midges at the relevant stages of their lifecycle.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has also installed bright spotlights at the Pandan Reservoir pumping station and turn them on at night to attract the adult midges as they emerge from the reservoir.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: By keeping the midges within the reservoir area, PUB can then carry out targeted and effective measures, such as fogging at these spots.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This species exhibits different behaviours from other species.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, they hide in drains and culverts in the day and swarm above the drains in the evening.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has adapted by adding to the usual suite of measures.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They have greased the drain walls to trap the midges when they land to rest and have targeted these areas for fogging.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has explored the use of free-moving oily paper within drains to increase the capture rates of adult midges, which have worked very well, according to feedback from residents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This netting acts as a barrier to trap adult midges and reduces the number of adult midges that would otherwise be blown to the residential estate.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB has worked closely with West Coast Town Council to engage affected residents through multiple channels, such as dialogues, daily walkabouts and distribution of flyers, and has advised affected residents on the actions they can take within their premises, such as, switching off their lights when not in use, as midges are attracted to light, as well as installing insect screens at their windows or drawing their curtains, if necessary.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But at the end of the day, we have to recognise that man cannot control nature.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Midges cannot be eradicated as they are part of the natural aquatic ecosystem and will emerge to breed, especially when aided by favourable environmental conditions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Climate change, as mentioned, will further complicate our efforts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our reservoirs supply drinking water to the population and we have to be careful to ensure that – and this is important – PUB's mitigation measures, both short- and long-term, do not end up compromising water quality.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, PUB remains committed to working with the Town Councils and advisors to minimise public inconvenience caused.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While PUB will continue to find more effective mitigation measures, we also seek residents' understanding and tolerance, should they find these insects in their homes.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Before I raise my supplementary questions to the Minister, I would like to thank the PUB and Town Council teams for the very, very hard work in tackling the mass midge outbreak.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Speaker, since July this year, residents living near Pandan Reservoir have suffered greatly from the mass emergence of midges.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Their homes have been invaded by the midges.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Corridors, lifts and bus stops have been swamped.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Cars, buses, bicycles and motorbikes have been affected.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Some have likened it to being in a horror movie.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Seriously, if you have visited, it is really scary.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: There were some really great ideas that were shared and I would like to raise some for the Minister's consideration in my supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: First, whilst I appreciate that fogging has been proven to be an effective way to kill adult midges, there are concerns among our residents about the health risk from exposure to chemicals from sustained fogging, particularly as the outbreak has lasted for an extended period.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Second, as the Minister shared, the midges issue cannot be solved or eradicated permanently.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Third, the most effective way to deal with midges is to eliminate them at source.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I know PUB uses biological larvicide, bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (BTI), and using tonnes of it this time, at the reservoir, by injecting the larvicide into the reservoir's sediment.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: But despite all that, the problem appears to persist.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I get constant questions that I would like to ask the Minister: how does PUB determine the effectiveness of BTI in controlling the larva population at the reservoir?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: How can the injected BTI be expected to zero in on the midge larva, given the vast area of the reservoir sediment?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Fourth, besides installing nets at the reservoir to serve as barriers to midges flying towards the housing estate, I would like to ask if more trees and shrubs can be added to also serve as barriers and places for the midges to congregate, so that they do not go into people's homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think this is a great opportunity for us to go back to our biology lessons.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Like I mentioned before, this problem is really man versus nature, the kind of war man has never been known to win.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Indeed, we can only suppress, we can only do our best, but we have to live with nature.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition to using a safe pesticide, we also dilute it, dilute it a lot, so that in addition to just thinking about killing these pests, we also do not want to harm the workers who are using them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, they are used in a way, at a frequency that is known and recommended by WHO to be safe for humans, safe for the operators, as well as for the people that we are trying to help.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Once you own your property, you own your home, you have to do what you can to protect yourself.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sometimes, we have residents who came to get help, for example, on their leaking pipes or issues which are more pertinent to their own home living conditions.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Technically speaking, they should be taking care of these issues.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But I think there is no harm, we can see what we can do to help, certainly from the advisors themselves.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We can come together and look at what we can do, because this situation does not come all the time, not every year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, to put in something which would become a permanent fixture, this may also affect the kind of image that the reservoir or the places around the reservoir should be.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we have to be very careful about the kind of solutions we want to implement with or for them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is actually a naturally occurring bacteria, soil bacteria, which produces spores, which are toxic specifically to the digestive system of midge larvae.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As we put in the larvicide, we also monitor the quality of the water.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We cannot put so much to kill, just because there are more midges in the river.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the end, the quality of the water gets compromised.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, there is a tradeoff between killing enough, or killing too much and we end up killing ourselves.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is a limit to which these measures can mitigate the issues that residents are facing.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is a more beautiful way, definitely, than putting screens.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But is it an effective way to prevent the midges from coming into people's homes?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We do not want, in the end, to create new problems like people having different kinds of pests because of the kind of trees that we plant near their homes or around the reservoirs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My residents have been bringing up this issue on midges and mayflies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister, will PUB carry out preventive measures for Lower Seletar Reservoir before it becomes, like my Parliamentary colleague mentioned, a "horror movie scene"?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We do not want a sledgehammer for a small problem or small hammer for a big problem.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Part of the problem is climate change and something we cannot alter.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I was wondering whether we have looked at ways of changing the micro-climate around the reservoirs.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Because this only happens in certain reservoirs and I agree that it is because of the water.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But there have been some studies that looked at the vegetation and the micro-climate around the banks of the reservoirs.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I understand that this is part of nature.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: But for the community that is impacted by that, it is really bad.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: So, I would like to propose for the Minister's consideration and collaboration with maybe HDB and other agencies, given that this phenomenon cannot be eradicated.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must also take this into consideration for the kinds of things we have to spend for when we try to tackle bigger issues in the years to come when climate change is upon us.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have not really understood properly how it will affect Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: What the Prime Minister has mentioned are only those things that we know can happen and should start working on from now.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Issues around pests are, in fact, more dangerous and I will mention it in my next Parliamentary Question reply around mosquitoes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will see what we can do for localities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we also should know that our resources are limited.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to put focus on important areas and not over-promise on other areas, but rather to over-deliver.
